conceptsFound.steelman: A cut card should hold only what makes THIS cut different. Everything shared with its process family — chamber temp band, wrap behaviour, finish behaviour, rest, fuel class, doneness ladder shape — lives once in a named archetype. Adding a cut = pick archetype + write ~8 deltas. Adding a NEW parameter to the whole catalog = edit ~17 archetypes, not 279 cards.

headline: The owner's hypothesis is right, but the strongest argument for it is not the one he made. Compressing today's cards buys almost nothing in bytes — the DATA payload is 977 KB raw / ~174 KB gzipped inside a 7.78 MB / 2.18 MB bundle, and 54% of the cuts' weight is citations that must stay per-cut. What an archetype layer actually buys is the ability to ADD the proposal's new parameters at all: crispness, chewiness, glaze window, finish behaviour cannot be hand-authored 279 times, but they can be authored ~17 times. And the repetition is real and measurable — with a 19-template (cat, rule-class) key, 1,384 of 2,470 CUTS field slots (56.0%) equal their template's modal value. We have already proven this approach works twice, at full catalog scale: methodRules/itemStages store ZERO process shape per cut (130 cuts → 4 distinct valid-combo sets), and equipment_map.py derives equipment for all 279 recipes with 0 hand-typed tokens (279 → 54 distinct shapes). The genuine defect the proposal exposes is the opposite of bloat: our most important process parameter, the stall wrap, is NOT stored as data at all — the `wrap` field is dead (127/130 = 'לא', never read by app.js) and the real decision sits in Hebrew prose inside `somid` for 24 cuts, recovered only by a regex in equipment_map.
whereItBeatsUs:
Three places, plainly.

**1. `Wrap_Stage` is a parameter in the proposal; in our system it is a sentence.** §3.1 lists `Wrap_Stage` and §4.5 emits a `THE_STALL_WRAP` stage with a material and a trigger temperature. Our `data.py` CUTS field `wrap` is dead weight: 127/130 cuts hold 'לא', and `grep` over app.js for `c.wrap` returns nothing but a DOM variable at app.js:2533. The actual wrap decision — "עטיפה ב-70°C" — is free Hebrew prose inside `somid` on 24 cuts. `equipment_map.py::_wrap_gear` (line 198) recovers the butcher-paper/foil requirement for those 24 cuts by regex over that prose; **0 cuts get it from the `wrap` field**. So the single most consequential process parameter in low-and-slow BBQ is, in our data model, an unparseable string that the equipment deriver has to reverse-engineer. `itemStages()` (app.js:4093) therefore cannot emit a wrap stage, the scheduler cannot alert on it, and the string costs 24 AI translations per language across a 23-language queue.

**2. Its parameters are enums; ours are free text, so nothing can reason over them.** §3.1 defines `P_MOIST_ENV` (DRY|WET|VACUUM) and `P_FINISH` (GRILL_HIGH|OVEN_BROIL|FLAMBE|NONE). Our equivalents are `sear` — 25 distinct free-text values over 130 cuts, 22 of them singletons like 'גריל קמור-למטה' and 'הרתחה/אידוי→גריל' — and `mid`, 22 distinct values. `soTreatText(c.somid)` at app.js:1585 string-matches a couple of them; everything else is rendered as prose and nothing branches on it. This is why we cannot answer "will this come out chewy?" — we never encoded the answer as a value.

**3. It states archetype+delta as a first principle; we arrived at it by accident, unevenly.** §1.1 says outright: 95 of 100 brisket recipes are the same variables re-combined. We *do* this for process shape and equipment, brilliantly — and *don't* for the cut card itself, and the inconsistency is measurable drift. Within the 13 collagen beef cuts: `לחי בקר` (smt 105), `שריר בקר/אוסובוקו` (110) and `זנב שור` (110) all cite the **same source**, "AmazingRibs — Slow Smoked Chuck Roast (collagen-cut analog)", with three different chamber temperatures. `אסאדו` (105) vs `אונטרייב` and `שפונדרה` (110) all cite "AmazingRibs — Texas Beef Short Ribs". Same citation, different number. Same in SPECIALS: 32 cold-smoked cheeses split across smt 25 / 28 / 30 with no class distinction visible. An archetype layer makes that class of drift structurally impossible.
whereWeAreBetter:
**Process shape is already fully compressed, and the proposal's own code is not.** `methodRules()` (app.js:989) classifies every cut into one of 5 rule classes purely from `cat`, `doneness` and `eng` — no per-cut rule data exists. `validCombo()` (app.js:1041) then collapses 130 cuts into exactly **4 distinct valid-combo sets** (65 / 37 / 27 / 1 cuts). `itemStages()` (app.js:4093) generates the entire stage sequence from the profile plus the chosen path and order; not one stage list is stored. `MAKE_COOK` (app.js:3707) covers 102 makes with **9 shared cook profiles**. Meanwhile the proposal's `Validate_Equipment_For_Cut` in §4.3 opens with `IF CUT == "Brisket"` — hardcoding per-cut equipment alternatives, which is exactly the duplication §1.1 argues against. It preaches the compression; we shipped it.

**Equipment derivation is our proof at full scale.** `equipment_map.py` tags all 279 recipes from what the recipe already encodes (casing/grind/cure/smt/svt/age/sear/kg), with **0 hand-typed tokens and 1 uncovered item** (halloumi). 279 recipes yield **54 distinct equipment shapes** — 19%. The `spec` block even carries the derived numbers (`footprint_cm2` on all 130 cuts, `casing_mm` on 71, `rh_pct` on 27). Nothing in the proposal demonstrates derivation at this scale.

**Our flavour layer is already the proposal's §7, and further along.** All **354** seasonings declare `cats` protein compatibility; `SEASONING_TAGS` adds flavor/base/heat; `HOUSE_RUB_MAP` maps all 130 cuts to **17** distinct house rubs; the compatibility gate is live at app.js:1297. The proposal offers three profiles in a table.

**The boilerplate is already squeezed out of our prose.** Of 3,677 distinct catalog prose strings per language, masking every number leaves 3,554 shapes — only **123 (3.3%)** are number-only variants of another, and only 5% share a five-word opening. The generators (`SG()` for all 52 new sausages, `b_*`/`sausage_*`/`bacon`/`cheese_cold` for 52 more) already did that work: 332 of 807 phase instructions (41%) are exact duplicates, collapsed to one dictionary key. I will not claim prose compression is available — it is not.

**And the honest limit on the whole idea, which I would rather state than have found later: this saves almost no bytes.** DATA = 977 KB raw / ~174 KB gzipped inside a 7.78 MB / 2.18 MB bundle (12.5% / 8%). Of the cuts' 334 KB: 182 KB citations, 60 KB derived equip, only **92 KB authored fields**. Halving the authored fields saves ~46 KB raw, ~8 KB gzipped — 0.4% of the bundle. Anyone selling this on payload is selling the wrong thing.
proposedModel:
**A build-time archetype layer. Not a runtime indirection.** The single design decision that makes this cheap: `archetypes.py` expands into fully-populated dicts during `build.py`, before `payload` is assembled. `itemStages`, `effectiveSchedule`, `comboMethodEntry`, `equipment_map.apply`, `eqmValidity` and every render site keep seeing exactly the dict shape they see today. No new runtime layer, no new read-path to test, no i18n surface.

**1. `archetypes.py` — ~17 archetypes, named from what is actually in the data**

Cuts (from the (cat, rule-class) grouping that scored 56.0%):
`AR_COLLAGEN_LOWSLOW` (37) · `AR_STEAK_REVERSE` (~30, red 5-level ladder) · `AR_POULTRY_DARK` (8) · `AR_POULTRY_WHITE` (2) · `AR_SEAFOOD_FAST` (15) · `AR_FISH_GENTLE` (5) · `AR_PRODUCE_GRILL` (27) · `AR_OFFAL_FAST` (11) · `AR_OFFAL_PRETENDERIZE` (1, gizzard).
Specials: `AR_COLD_SMOKE_CHEESE` (32) · `AR_JERKY_DRY` (3) · `AR_BACON_CURE_SMOKE` (2) · `AR_SEMI_DRY_SMOKED_SAUSAGE` (4) · `AR_DRY_FERMENT_SAUSAGE` (5).
Makes: reuse the 9 existing `MAKE_COOK` categories — already an archetype table; just move it next to the others.

```python
ARCHETYPES = {
 "AR_COLLAGEN_LOWSLOW": dict(
    ruleClass="collagen",                      # feeds methodRules() — replaces its cat/doneness sniffing
    smt=110, sot=110, svt=68, tgt=95, rest=30,
    moist="DRY",                               # P_MOIST_ENV enum
    wrap=dict(atC=70, material="paper"),       # STRUCTURED — see §3
    finish="NONE",                             # P_FINISH enum
    shapeClass="slab",                         # already used by equipment_map._shape
    coalClass="long-burn",                     # replaces the per-cut brand string
    woodFamily=["oak","hickory"],
 ),
 "AR_COLD_SMOKE_CHEESE": dict(
    ruleClass="coldsmoke", smt=28, smhDefault="2", tgt=None,
    prep="fridge-dry-overnight", ageRest="2w-fridge",
    maxChamberC=30,                            # ONE rule, not 33 warning sentences
 ),
 ...
}
```

**2. Cut record — archetype id + delta only**

```python
dict(n=1, heb="בריסקט", eng="Brisket", cat="בקר",
     arch="AR_COLLAGEN_LOWSLOW",
     d=dict(smt=105, svh="30", smh="3", soh="12", kg=5.5, wood="אלון/היקורי"),
     safe=63,                                   # NEVER inherited — see §4
     doneness=None,
     rubId="rub-dalmatian",                     # replaces the 105-distinct free-text `rub`
     src={...})
```

Delta shape: `d` carries **only** keys whose value differs from the archetype. Expected size from the measurement: median ~8 of 19 fields, because 56.0% of slots inherit.

**3. Promote three things out of prose into structure — this is the real win**

- `wrap: {atC:int, material:'paper'|'foil'|'none'}` — parse the 24 `somid` wrap sentences once, into data. `equipment_map._wrap_gear(...)` then reads `c['wrap']['material']` instead of regexing Hebrew, and `itemStages()` gains a real `kind:'wrap'` stage that the scheduler and the work plan can render and alert on.
- `finish: 'GRILL_HIGH'|'PAN_SEAR'|'BROIL'|'TORCH'|'STEAM'|'NONE'` + optional `finishNote` — replaces `sear` (25 free-text values → 6 enum + note). 73.1% inheritable.
- `midTreat: 'NONE'|'CHILL'|'SKIN_DRY'|'BLANCH'|'GLAZE'|'SOAK'` + optional `midNote` — replaces `mid` (22 values, 79× 'אין'). 75.4% inheritable.

Plus two pure shrinks: `doneness: {scale:'red5', base:50, gaps:[4,6,4,4]}` (20.3% of authored bytes → 3 tokens; 6 shapes cover all 56 cuts) and drop `saved` entirely — compute `soh_upper − smh_upper` (exact on 49/130, within 0.5 h on 115/130, median error 0.05 h) or, if the 15 outliers are cited, keep `saved` only in `d` for those 15.

**4. The safety firewall — explicit, and testable**

```python
NEVER_INHERITED = {"safe", "tgt", "svt", "svh", "smt", "smh", "sot", "soh", "src"}
```
Two-tier: fields in `NEVER_INHERITED` may appear in an archetype as a **default that a cut must restate to accept** — i.e. `resolve()` raises unless the cut either supplies the value in `d` or carries `inherit=["smt"]` naming it explicitly. Nothing safety- or schedule-bearing is ever silently inherited. `safe` (6 distinct values over 130) stays fully explicit per cut, per `docs/sources/baldwin-backbone.md`. A build guard — call it Guard D, sibling of A/B/C — fails if any `safe` value materializes from an archetype rather than the cut.

**5. Citations: normalize the ref, never the note**

```python
SOURCE_REFS = {"S_PROTOCOL_PRODUCE": dict(ref="Protocol — produce", url=...),
               "S_BALDWIN_POULTRY":  dict(ref="Baldwin/USDA poultry floor", url=...), ...}
```
875 instances → 546 distinct refs; the `safe` slot alone is 130 → **38**. Per-cut `src` becomes `{"safe": {"refId":"S_BALDWIN_POULTRY", "note":"…"}}`. The `note` — 793 distinct of 875, 91% unique — stays verbatim, per cut, untouched. Cuts' citations are 182 KB of their 334 KB; this recovers most of it while making a source URL fix a one-line edit instead of 26.

**6. Migration — three phases, each with a byte-identical gate**

- **P1 (zero behaviour change).** Write `archetypes.py` + `resolve(record)`. Derive archetype defaults mechanically from current modal values. Gate: `json.dumps(resolved_payload) == json.dumps(current_payload)`, byte for byte. Any mismatch is a real inconsistency and gets escalated to the owner, not smoothed over. This is the RED/GREEN and it is a single test.
- **P2 (shrink).** Delete inherited fields from the 279 records, keeping only `d`. Same byte-identical gate. `npx playwright test` unchanged, 816 green.
- **P3 (the payoff).** Add the proposal's new parameters — `crispness`, `chewRisk`, `glazeWindowMin`, `finishTexture` — to the ~17 archetypes, with per-cut overrides only where cited. This is the phase that is impossible without P1/P2, and it is the whole reason to do this.

**7. The drift audit is a prerequisite, not a follow-up.** Before any modal value becomes an archetype default, the 105/110 collagen-beef split and the 25/28/30 cheese split must be resolved against their citations — `לחי בקר`, `שריר בקר` and `זנב שור` cite the identical source with different chamber temps. Picking a modal value without resolving that would silently change a cited schedule, which DoD-10 forbids.
openQuestions: The drift is provable but its cause is not: `לחי בקר` (smt 105), `שריר בקר/אוסובוקו` (110) and `זנב שור` (110) all cite the SAME source, 'AmazingRibs — Slow Smoked Chuck Roast (collagen-cut analog)'. Same for `אסאדו` (105) vs `אונטרייב`/`שפונדרה` (110) on 'AmazingRibs — Texas Beef Short Ribs'. Is 105 vs 110 a real distinction someone made deliberately, or authoring noise? Nothing in the data or the citation notes says. This must be answered per group before a modal value can become an archetype default — otherwise P1's byte-identical gate is the only thing standing between us and a silent schedule change.

May a `safe` value ever be inherited? 26 produce cuts share the identical citation 'Protocol — produce' and the identical value 0; 15 poultry cuts share 'Baldwin/USDA poultry floor'. Inheriting them would be safe in fact and would remove a copy-paste class of error — but `docs/sources/baldwin-backbone.md` says every `safe` value traces to a cited primary source, and my proposed Guard D forbids it. This is a §4 waiver-gate question and needs the owner in conversation, not a plan file.

What is the escape hatch for a genuine misfit? `גבינת שמנת מעושנת` sits in the cheese group at smt=110 °C — hot-smoked — against 32 cold-smoked neighbours at ≤30 °C. Does it get `arch:null` and a full explicit record, an archetype of one, or an override so large the archetype adds nothing? Getting this wrong is how archetype layers become worse than the duplication they replaced.

Does an archetype ever become user-visible? If a card says 'קולגן — עישון איטי' that is a new string, and with a 23-language queue and Guard A enforcing every active language, a user-facing archetype name is a real cost. My proposal keeps them internal (build-time only, never rendered) — but the moment CP2's path panel or the AI grounding wants to say 'this cut follows the collagen archetype', that changes.

Should the archetype own `ruleClass` outright, replacing `methodRules()`'s current sniffing of `cat`/`doneness`/`eng`? It would be cleaner and explicit — but `methodRules` is load-bearing for `validCombo` → `itemProfile` → `itemPaths` → `eqmValidity` → the E3 event gate, and per Chesterton's Fence I would want to see the 4 valid-combo sets reproduced exactly before touching it. Recommend deferring to P2 at the earliest.

How much of the 56.0% inheritance figure is an artifact of my (cat, rule-class) key rather than a real process family? The key is a proxy I chose; the (cat)-only key scored 49.4% with 13 templates and (rule-class)-only scored 42.1% with 4. A hand-curated archetype set could plausibly beat 56% or could fall short of it — the number is a floor for a mechanical key, not a measured ceiling.
